appearance_facts.fact: Chrome bar (orange) is the leftmost; its top sits just above the 50 gridline.
Safari bar (dark blue) is the second bar; its top sits just above the 60 gridline and is the tallest bar on the page.
Edge bar (light blue) is the third bar; its top sits just above the 40 gridline.
Firefox bar (orange-yellow) is the fourth bar; its top is just below the 10 gridline.
Others bar (crimson) is the rightmost; its top is just below the 10 gridline and slightly lower than the Firefox bar.
Bold percentage labels sit above each bar: 38% (Chrome), 44% (Safari), 44% (Edge), 4% (Firefox), 10% (Others).

printed_facts.fact: Categories left-to-right: Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox, Others.

public_definitions: user_goal: 'Review the browser usage-share dashboard, then assign additional support capacity to the browser with the highest current market_share.'
policy row: 'Support capacity rule — Select the browser with the highest current market_share'.
option_labels: 'Assign additional support capacity to Edge' / '...to Safari' / '...to Chrome'.
uncertain: Safari and Edge both carry the printed annotation '44%'; the visual bar heights differ (Safari taller), so the printed values are internally inconsistent with the bar geometry and the exact tie-break is unresolved.
The printed percentages (38+44+44+4+10 = 140) do not sum to 100, so the dashboard values are not a consistent share set; the highest-value reading is taken literally from the annotations.
